name: microtome-ribbon-feed
title: Microtome Ribbon Feed
description: A full-bleed hero built on a rotary-microtome sectioning mechanic: a block reciprocates onto a fixed blade every stroke, each cut section clings to the last, and an unbroken ribbon of sections grows off the blade tip and drapes under its own weight.
instruction: Build <MicrotomeRibbonFeed children? className?> as a full-bleed 2D-canvas hero rendering a rotary microtome's sectioning mechanic. THE CHAIN: the ribbon is a verlet point chain pinned at index 0 to a fixed anchor (the blade tip, at 0.3w/0.24h). Every STROKE_INTERVAL_S=1.4s, at DWELL_PHASE=0.5 of the stroke clock, splice a new point into index 1 (immediately after the anchor) rather than appending to the end — this is the freshly cut section, physically nearest the blade, and it pushes every previously-cut point one slot further from the anchor exactly as a real ribbon's older sections get shouldered away by whatever is cut after them. Each frame: integrate all points but the anchor with verlet (velocity = (pos - prevPos) * DAMPING=0.985, plus GRAVITY_PX_S2=900 scaled by containerMinDim/1080 and dt^2), then run CONSTRAINT_ITERS=4 passes of a distance constraint holding consecutive points at SEG_LEN_REF=6px (scaled the same way) apart, re-pinning index 0 to the anchor after every pass. No easing curve is scripted for the drape — the catenary sag is the constraint solve settling under gravity, which is why fresh segments near the blade stay taut and only the older, farther segments visibly sag. STROKE + CUT SHARE ONE CLOCK: strokeClock = (strokeClock + dt/STROKE_INTERVAL_S) % 1 is the only timer; the block's reciprocating bob (BLOCK_TRAVEL_REF=46px scaled, eased sin(t*pi/2) down 0..DWELL_PHASE, eased return DWELL_PHASE..1) and the segment-splice both read this same value, so the cut always visibly lands at the moment the block reaches the blade — never two independent timers that happen to roughly agree. CAP AND RESET: once segment count (points.length-1) reaches MAX_SEGMENTS=60, start a FADE_S=2s alpha fade on the whole ribbon draw pass, then reset points back to a single anchor point and resume growth — an unbounded loop, never a process that finishes and stops. POINTER: pointer position (canvas-local, tracked via pointermove/pointerleave) applies a small outward nudge (POINTER_FORCE=5.5, scaled) to any chain point within POINTER_RADIUS_REF=90px (scaled), falloff-squared by distance, added directly into stepChain before the constraint solve — a physical sway, not a decorative overlay — and independently brightens nearby seam-tick alpha from 0.35 up to 0.85 as a luminance-only glint (never touches --ns-accent or mixes any hue). Pointer input must never change strokeClock or segment cadence. SEAMS: at every interior point, draw a short perpendicular tick (segLen*0.4 long) in --ns-muted so consecutive sections read as discrete joins, not one smooth blurred line — this is what keeps the ribbon legible as sectioning rather than a generic wavy stroke. TOKENS: --foreground for the block, blade and ribbon stroke, --ns-muted for seam ticks, read via getComputedStyle(document.documentElement) at mount before any paint, re-read on a MutationObserver watching documentElement's class/data-theme plus a prefers-color-scheme change listener. No color literals, no hue math anywhere — brightening is alpha only. HOST: ResizeObserver on the root element (not window.resize) recomputes w/h/dpr (capped 2) and the anchor position, and re-pins the existing chain's anchor point to the new location rather than leaving it stale; an IntersectionObserver (threshold 0) and visibilitychange both pause the single rAF loop; unmount cancels the frame and disconnects every observer/listener. prefers-reduced-motion (checked via matchMedia, live via a change listener) replaces the rAF loop with a deterministic replay: tick() is stepped at a fixed SUBSTEP=1/90 from a freshly reset chain up to STATIC_TIME_S = 22*1.4 + 1.4*0.5 + 0.2 (~31.5s) and drawn once — since growth has no randomness at all, this reproduces the exact same ~22-segment frame (fresh sections taut near the blade, a 23rd about to be cut, older segments in full catenary drape, block at the blade) every time it is called, including on resize and theme flips in the reduced-motion path. children render as ordinary DOM (eyebrow/headline/CTA) positioned over the canvas, unlike a rasterized-into-canvas headline, since nothing here needs the ribbon to occlude or emboss the type.
useWhen: Pick microtome-ribbon-feed when the hero should read as one continuous mechanical process building itself over time — a growing, draping chain with a legible per-segment cadence. Pick kymograph-smoke-trace instead when the mechanic should be a permanent scratched trace on a recirculating drum rather than a growing physical chain; weld-pool when the hero's headline itself needs to be lit and dented as part of a molten surface.
